paper: Grimm & Eaves 2025, Accurate Numerical Simulations of Open Quantum Systems Using Spectral Tensor Trains
replication_verdict: REPLICATED (core analytic anchor, Eqs. 16-17); PARTIAL for paper overall
notes: Open questions are grounded in what this replication validated (Eqs. 15-17, extrinsic-Markov SLE -> Lindblad) vs. what it did NOT touch (STT machinery, intrinsic-noise kernel of App. A, memory scaling of Fig. 4, barren-plateau training of Fig. 5).

open_questions.q: Does the reported Q-ASPEN memory scaling p~2.0 vs PT-TEMPO p~8.3 on the 2-32 site extrinsic-noise chain (Fig. 4) actually hold under an independent re-implementation of the STT compression, or is it artifact of specific hyperparameters (Chebyshev rank, bond dimension truncation, SGD schedule)?
open_questions.basis: This replication explicitly did not touch C4. REPORT.md sec. 4 marks it 'out of scope' and only verified the exact analytic limit (C1). The p~2.0 vs p~8.3 gap is the paper's main practical selling point over PT-TEMPO but is entirely untested by an independent group.
next_steps: Port the STT construction from Eqs. 10-14 (matrix-product of Chebyshev-expanded K_alpha(omega)) in a fresh codebase.
Run OQuPy/PT-TEMPO on the same 2-32 site chain geometry and record peak RSS + wallclock per site count.
Fit log-log slope p on both methods across at least 5 chain lengths with fixed bond-dim/rank policy.
Sweep STT bond dimension and Chebyshev rank to see how sensitive p is to those hyperparameters.

open_questions.q: For the intrinsic-noise (thermal/quantum) regime governed by the App. A influence kernel obeying fluctuation-dissipation, does Q-ASPEN reproduce PT-TEMPO on the biased-qubit spin-boson model of Fig. 3 to within a numerically meaningful tolerance across a range of bath temperatures and coupling strengths (not just the published operating point)?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md is explicit: 'geometry mimicked, not the intrinsic-noise bath'. Our SLE-MC used white extrinsic noise, so 'matches Fig. 3' in our runs means SLE-MC matches our own Lindblad, not that either matches the published spin-boson curve. C3 remains untested independently.
next_steps: Implement the App. A kernel with correct FDT weights for a Drude-Lorentz or ohmic bath.
Reproduce Fig. 3 exactly using the paper's stated spectral density and beta.
Sweep beta and coupling (weak -> intermediate) and overlay Q-ASPEN, PT-TEMPO, and (where available) HEOM.
Report L2 and L-infinity deviations of the population and coherence trajectories, not just visual agreement.

open_questions.q: Is the barren-plateau training obstruction of Fig. 5 a generic property of STT-parameterized influence kernels, or is it specific to the SGD/importance-sampling recipe used in the paper?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md marks C5 as 'not tested here' and calls it a training pathology orthogonal to correctness. The paper reports the plateau but does not benchmark against alternative optimizers or initialization schemes; this is a load-bearing usability question because a method that is exact in the limit but untrainable in practice is not competitive.
next_steps: Measure the empirical gradient-norm distribution per STT layer under SGD, Adam, and natural-gradient/K-FAC on a small system.
Try Xavier/spectral-norm initializations designed to avoid barren plateaus in tensor networks.
Test whether layer-wise pretraining or Riemannian optimization on the tangent space of low-rank tensor manifolds circumvents the plateau.
Report a plateau severity metric (variance of gradient norm vs. depth/width) that can be compared across methods.

open_questions.q: How does Q-ASPEN behave at the crossover from Markovian to strongly non-Markovian noise (finite correlation time tau_c comparable to system timescales), where the extrinsic-Markov limit that anchors correctness (Eqs. 15-17) no longer applies?
open_questions.basis: The replication anchor is precisely the delta-correlated limit <xi(t)xi(s)> = gamma delta(t-s). Everything the STT is doing that PT-TEMPO cannot is presumably in the colored/non-Markovian regime where the influence kernel G is nontrivial. The paper's Fig. 3 tests one such geometry but the systematic behavior across correlation times is not mapped, and this replication only touched the Markov corner.
next_steps: Drive the biased qubit with exponentially correlated noise xi(t) with tunable tau_c and compare Q-ASPEN vs. direct SLE-MC (which stays exact).
Sweep tau_c/T_sys from 0.01 to 10 and log the STT bond-dim needed for a fixed target error.
Identify the correlation-time regime where the STT bond-dim grows and see whether that boundary aligns with the paper's stated regime of validity.

open_questions.q: Does the method conserve complete positivity of the reduced density matrix under STT truncation, or only trace? Trace-preservation is easy; complete positivity is what distinguishes a physically valid open-system propagator.
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md verifies Tr(rho_MC) = 1.0000 across all three qubit cases (C2), but this is trace preservation, not complete positivity. In the exact Lindblad limit (Eq. 17) CP is guaranteed by construction (Lindblad form). Under finite STT bond-dim truncation this guarantee is not obvious and the paper does not (per what is summarized in REPORT.md) present a proof or systematic test of CP preservation.
next_steps: Diagonalize rho at each timestep of Q-ASPEN runs and record min eigenvalue as a function of bond-dim and t.
Construct the Choi matrix of the effective STT propagator on small systems and test positive-semidefiniteness.
Compare CP-violation magnitude of Q-ASPEN vs. truncated TEMPO under matched compression budgets.
If CP violations exist, quantify whether they vanish as bond-dim -> full rank.
